Lessons.Title: Compare and Order Decimals
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: You will compare and order decimals.
Key idea: Order decimal values by corresponding whole-number, tenths and hundredths places, including exact ties.
How to reason: Align values to hundredths when useful and compare from greatest place value left to right.
Source-inspired opening: Warm-up:  Estimation Exploration	 (10 minutes). Use the teacher-provided mathematical representations and explain how different valid answers arise.

Activity 1:  All in Order	 (15 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as 1.08, 0.08, 0.80, 0.9. First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.

Activity 2:  400-Meter Dash in a Flash	 (20 minutes): apply the learning goal to quantities such as The table shows eight of the top runners in the Women’s 400-Meter event. Their best running times, listed here, put the runners in the world’s top 25 for this event., 48.37, 49.3, 48.7. First-party discussion supports clear strategies and comparisons, while original drawings and classroom materials are teacher-led.
Original source Cool-down is access-restricted/unverified; Edulytics substitutes goal-aligned independently authored teacher-reviewed exit prompt.
Edulytics worked model: Compare 0.9 and 0.8 by writing each in hundredths.. Explain every transformation and check using equal wholes/units.
Open reflection: Original six-number source sets and 400-metre track record table require full teacher review.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming longer written decimals must be greater, for example 0.45 versus 0.9.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: It does not preserve the intended mathematical relationship or original task condition.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Align values to hundredths when useful and compare from greatest place value left to right.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Claiming 0.59 exceeds 0.62 because the digit 9 is larger than 2.
